chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Harun ib Muslim from Ali ib al-Hakam from al-Husayn ib al-Hasan al-Kindi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Indeed, a man tells a lie, and is thereby deprived of the prayer of the night; and when he is deprived of the prayer of the night, he is thereby deprived of sustenance."
ai.seo_question: How does lying affect a person's sustenance and night prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the metaphysical consequence of falsehood, positing that a single lie severs the connection to *Salat al-Layl*, the prayer of the righteous. This deprivation of night worship is not merely a loss of reward but a causal mechanism that restricts *Rizq* (divine sustenance), illustrating how spiritual discipline directly influences material and spiritual blessings.
